description: Reference performance and size data for NIST-standardised post-quantum algorithms and the classical algorithms they replace. Used when liboqs is not installed and as the baseline shown next to live measurements.

sources.FIPS-203: NIST FIPS 203, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard (ML-KEM), August 2024. Key and ciphertext sizes.
sources.FIPS-204: NIST FIPS 204, Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard (ML-DSA), August 2024. Key and signature sizes.
sources.issue-17-reference: Timing figures supplied in project issue #17, attributed there to NIST PQC round 3/4 reference benchmarks (CRYSTALS-Kyber / CRYSTALS-Dilithium, x86-64 AVX2 class hardware). Indicative, not re-measured.
sources.derived-liboqs-ratio: ML-DSA-65 figures from issue #17 scaled by the ML-DSA-87 / ML-DSA-65 ratios measured with liboqs 0.16.0 (x86-64 Linux, 20 iterations): keygen x1.34, sign x1.50, verify x1.80. Keeps the issue's hardware baseline while using measured relative cost.
sources.estimate: Order-of-magnitude estimate for OpenSSL-class implementations on comparable x86-64 hardware. Not a citation. Cross-checked against live runs on Windows and Linux (WSL2) hosts, where measured values differed by up to ~3x between environments; run a live benchmark for numbers on your own hardware.
sources.SP-800-57: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1, security strengths of classical algorithms.

tls_model.description: Assumptions for the migration impact calculator (TLS 1.3, server-authenticated handshake).

ECDSA-P256.size_source: SEC 1 uncompressed point; raw r||s signature

ECDH-P256.size_source: SEC 1 uncompressed point (TLS key_share). encaps = ephemeral keygen + derive; decaps = derive.
